text: At 65 minutes, Kingsmoor FC triggered a high press by increasing PPDA from 8.0 to 7.6 and raised their defensive line (line height 0.5 to 0.62), adopting a more aggressive pressing trigger to force turnovers in advanced areas [#1187]. Concurrently, they increased directness in build-up play (0.5 to 0.65), enhancing verticality to exploit rapid transitions against Westport Albion’s compact 4-4-2. This shift created an overload in transitional moments, doubling high turnovers (2 to 4) and increasing box touches (10 to 12), but at the cost of reducing possession (57.6% to 51.6%) and failing to generate shots or xG, reflecting challenges in converting pressure into quality chances. Meanwhile, Westport Albion’s xG dropped from 0.74 to 0.63, showing some disruption to their direct vertical passing style, but Kingsmoor struggled to capitalize immediately on the field tilt maintained around 67%.
